newsItems.text: BREAKING NEWS: Almere clinic reports record number of heat-related illnesses during summer months.
Dating app adds 'housing compatibility' feature for couples planning to combine units.
Housing waitlist reaches 18,000 as population growth outpaces construction.
Import delays extend to 12 weeks as global shipping networks remain disrupted.
Coastal districts relocate 500 residents as sea levels reach new historic high.
School children learn swimming before walking to navigate neighborhood canals.
Morning commute by canal boat delayed due to energy barge traffic at district hub.
Grandmother's vintage sewing machine valued higher than new electronics at local market.
Children's soccer league postpones matches due to park flooding - players to use elevated courts instead.
CITY-WIDE ALERT: Lithium-ion battery recycling now mandatory for all residents as critical shortages worsen. Drop-off points at Urban Commons hubs are reportedly overwhelmed.
HEALTH ADVISORY: PFA contamination levels in Weerwater have spiked again following recent floods. Residents are reminded that only water from designated purification towers is safe for consumption.
SPONGE PARK STATUS: City engineers report sponge parks are at 98% saturation after an overnight deluge. While central districts remain dry, the system is at its limit.
CONSTRUCTION HALTED: Work on the new Flevo Hospital wing has stopped due to a critical sand shortage. Officials are prioritizing sand for flood defense reinforcement.
BLACK MARKET: A black market for imported cotton has surged as local textile production struggles to meet demand. Authorities warn against counterfeit fabrics.
RE:FLEX HOUSING: The re:flex housing portal crashed from high traffic as thousands applied for new 'Reclaim' units on the old Rabobank tower.

CARBON PASSPORT ALERT: The carbon passport system has flagged over 2,000 residents for excessive energy consumption this quarter. Those affected face a temporary suspension of personal vehicle charging privileges.
BIOCYCLE HUB SUCCESS: The biocycle hub in district B-2 reports record methane generation from organic waste, securing the district's energy independence for the fifth consecutive month.
PUBLIC SAFETY WARNING: A parasitic fungus has been detected in the edible streetscape along the Landdrostdreef. Foraging in the area is strictly prohibited until further notice.
VERTICAL FARM OFFLINE: Vertical Farm #4 is offline for emergency maintenance, causing city-wide vegetable shortages. Salads have been temporarily removed from public canteen menus.
